reason: Both conversations correctly asked what the smell was like first and, once 'hot plastic/electrical' was described, issued a clear stop-and-unplug instruction and referred to an engineer; neither asked for make/model/serial, so neither surfaced the Beko fire-risk safety notice, which is the key missed escalation in both. Conversation 2 edges ahead because its first turn also efficiently checked for tripping and plug/socket scorching, and its safety stop explicitly told her not to open the back panel or test electrics herself, matching the safety boundary more fully. Conversation 1 was equally firm on stopping use but added speculative component lists without further practical guidance; the difference is minor.
